subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should OpenClaw expose `captionedFinalText` as a durable public channel-plugin capability, rather than keep this repair Telegram-owned until a wider channel contract is agreed?
rationale: The capability changes final-mode TTS delivery semantics for every current or future channel plugin that opts in, so code review cannot determine the intended permanent SDK boundary alone.

options.title: Accept the capability and require proof
options.body: Retain the generic capability, document its opt-in contract, and require current-head Telegram proof for every newly deferred delivery path before merge.

options.title: Narrow to Telegram
options.body: Move the immediate repair behind Telegram-owned behavior and track a separate SDK proposal if broader channel opt-in is not yet desired.

options.title: Defer the change
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers decide the long-term channel delivery API and fallback guarantees.

recommendation.title: Accept the capability and require proof
recommendation.body: Retain the generic capability, document its opt-in contract, and require current-head Telegram proof for every newly deferred delivery path before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history and the recorded project discussion connect this person most closely to the ACP, channel-capability, and Telegram/plugin boundary involved.
